To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the error probability is the dominant factor in determining the achievable rate of a delay-constrained system and 2) the error probability should be optimized jointly with the network sum rate to achieve the maximum throughput.

(a) in delay-constrained wireless networks, optimizing the peruser error probability in addition to the sum rate can significantly improve the network performance, and (b) the achievable rate of finite-length cod- words can be efficiently computed using the divide-and-con- quer technique.

the following questions: (i) How to design an algorithm to optimize the sum rate and error probability in down link wireless networks?
the design of the optimal transmission strategy in the downlink of a network with a finite-length codebook and finite blocklength, which is of great importance in practice.
the joint optimization of the sum rate and error probability in wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in delayconstrained scenarios, optimizing per-user error probability is a key to achieve high throughput.
, in a delay-constrained scenario, the per-user error rate should be minimized, and this will result in a high sum rate.

the finite blocklength effect has a significant impact on the system performance in terms of both the achievable rate and the error performance, especially for the systems with a large number of users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the finite-blocklength regime, the system performance is not only a function of the channel conditions but also a function of the delay constraint.

, in finite blocklength regime, we can simultaneously optimize the sum rate and error probability of the network, and the error probability is the key factor in achieving high throughput in delay-constrained systems.
, in delay-limited networks, the sum rate can be improved by optimizing the per-user probability of error.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the finite blocklength regime, optimizing the sum rate and minimizing the per-user error probabilities are not necessarily conflicting goals, and in some cases, the sum-rate performance of a network can be improved by increasing the error probabilities of some users.
the sum rate and error probability can be simultaneously optimized to maximize the system performance in the finite blocklength regime.
, by jointly optimizing the network sum rate, the error probability and the codeword lengths, it is possible to achieve a high throughput with low error probability.
